_version: What your game SAYS it is. scry never copies this onto your store row — it serves it beside the version actually published in the depot and flags the gap, because a tag ahead of a build is a signal and a typed field would erase it.

listing.name: Your Game
listing.blurb: The card's sentence: what the game is, in plain words. 400 characters.
listing.about: The long paragraph on the game page.

_listing: Every field a steward may write: name, kind, blurb, about, state, tags, repo, repo_public, room, play_url, capsule, hero, media, record, coins, collections, economy, receipts. The house keeps band, hidden, placeholder, lane and note — a game cannot commit its way onto a shelf. Drop this block entirely if a release only needs a post.

updates.title: The headline, 140 characters
updates.body: The update itself, in markdown. This lands in the store's feed and on your title's build record — the row the game page and the hub already render.

_updates: kind is one of update / patch / release / news / event. The `id` is yours and is what makes re-reading this file idempotent: an id that has already posted is skipped, so leaving old entries here is harmless. 20 per manifest. Write $SCRY as SCRY — a bare ticker; a $ is a shell variable and the two may not look alike.
_next: Fill this in, then: python3 sign_manifest.py --game your-slug   ...which writes scry.sig.json. Commit both. Keys starting with _ are your own margin notes and are ignored by scry. Full standard: https://scry.moreright.xyz/api/library/GAME-REPO.md
